findings.message: The new lines add a second ```sh fence inside the existing ```sh block under `# Observing`. The inner opening line is read as content and its closing fence ends the outer block. So `uv run clutch view status`, `view watch`, `view stats`, `view events`, and the `# Decisions` commands now render as prose, and the old closing ``` opens a stray code block that runs into `## VS Code extension`.
findings.paved_road: Remove the added inner fence lines and put `uv run clutch mcp serve  # run the stdio MCP server` as a plain line inside the existing ```sh block under `# Observing`.

findings.message: `clutch_stats` wraps all of `stats.collect_stats(...)` in `except ValueError` and maps it to `code="invalid_window"` with the road `use <N>h, <N>d, or <N>t`. `collect_stats` also raises ValueError subclasses that have nothing to do with the window, for example a pydantic `ValidationError` from `Invoice.model_validate_json` on a corrupt `checks.json`. Those get reported as a bad window, with a paved road that cannot fix them. The ticket asks for `stats.window_start` + `stats.collect_stats`, mapping only a bad window to `invalid_window`.
findings.paved_road: Call `stats.window_start(events, now, args.window)` first, inside the `except ValueError` that maps to `invalid_window` (as `handle_stats` does). Then call `collect_stats` outside that handler so other failures reach the general error mapping.
